step1_summary.chief_complaint: Swelling on the left elbow noticed about a week ago.
symptoms: Weird swelling on the left elbow for about a week
Not painful, but slightly warm to touch
Tenderness next to the swelling, but not on the tip of the elbow
No history of injury and can move the elbow normally
past_medical_history: Diagnosed with osteoarthritis a few years ago
family/social history: No known family history of rheumatology diseases
Runs 2-3 times a week, generally healthy
vital_signs/exam_findings: Swelling and warmth on the left elbow
Skin is a bit dry on the tip of the elbow
labs/imaging: Blood tests to be arranged: inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatological antibodies, and Gout check.

I: Infectious bursitis: Rationale includes warm, fluid-filled swelling that might indicate infection/inflammation of the elbow bursa.
Gout: Suggested by the possibility of fluid accumulation and swelling, though not commonly involved in elbow.
D: Osteoarthritis-related swelling: History of osteoarthritis could lead to joint changes and fluid buildup.
A: Bursitis: History and examination suggest an inflammation likely related to osteoarthritis. No systemic autoimmune disease is indicated currently.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: The clinical presentation of swelling, warmth, and tender fluid accumulation at the elbow strongly suggests bursitis, particularly since there is no systemic inflammation or infection noted.
supporting_evidence: Swelling and warmth localized to the elbow
opposing_evidence: Absence of systemic signs of infection or inflammation

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Considered due to localized warmth and swelling which can represent an infectious process in the bursa.
opposing_evidence: No systemic symptoms of infection (fevers, chills)
The doctor did not suspect septic arthritis

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: While gout can present with joint swelling and warmth, it more commonly affects the great toe and there is no history indicating high uric acid levels or episodes suggestive of gout.
supporting_evidence: Fluid-like swelling which could theoretically be monosodium urate crystal-related
opposing_evidence: No history of similar episodes or confirmation of hyperuricemia
